title: Who counts as a party for this question?
shortTitle: Who counts as a party for this question?
summary: Party status is sometimes context-dependent in representative litigation. Absent class members may be bound by a judgment while receiving different treatment from named parties for other procedural requirements.
notes: Mussat’s treatment of absentees for one jurisdictional purpose cannot simply be transferred to Article III injury or every other requirement.

sections.Meaning: Party status is sometimes context-dependent in representative litigation. Absent class members may be bound by a judgment while receiving different treatment from named parties for other procedural requirements.
sections.How to work through the question: Specify the legal consequence at issue rather than relying on the label party alone. Compare standing for damages, citizenship, venue, personal jurisdiction, participation, and the preclusive scope of a class judgment.
